description: Remove a solid or near-solid background from an image and return it as a transparent PNG. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/background-remover (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

colour.description: The background colour to remove, as #rrggbb hex. Omit to sample it from the four corners of the image; the response reports the colour used and whether the corners agreed on it.

data.description: The image file's bytes, base64-encoded. This removes a flat, single-colour background such as a white product shot or a scan; it is not a subject cutout for photos with busy backgrounds. Send the whole file as it is, up to 50 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/background-remover (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

feather.description: How soft the edge is, 0 to 100. It widens the band of partly transparent pixels around the tolerance threshold, as a percentage of tolerance; 0 gives a hard jagged cut.

name.description: The original filename. Used only to name the result, whose extension becomes .png because the output is always a PNG with transparency.

reach.description: edges (the default) removes only background connected to the image border, so enclosed areas like the hole in a letter or a window behind someone stay. everywhere removes every pixel within tolerance wherever it is.

tolerance.description: How far a pixel's colour may be from the background colour and still be removed, 0 to 100 as a share of the largest possible RGB distance. Raise it for uneven lighting or JPEG noise; too high eats into the subject.

type.description: The MIME type of the bytes in data: JPEG, PNG or WebP.

name: background_remover
title: Remove Background
